rfam.comment: This family represents the related mir-15a and mir-15b sequences. In humans miR-15a and miR-16 are clustered within 0.5 kb at 13q14. This region has been shown to be deleted in more than half of B cell chronic lymphocytic leukaemias (CLL). Both miR-15a and miR-16 are deleted or down-regulated in more than two thirds of CLL cases [2]. The mature sequence is excised from the 5' arm of the hairpin. The family represents the microRNA (miRNA) precursor mir-125 imported from miRBase [3].
